title: Route-profile identification and access preview
contract: Layout and frozen-run playback share profile labels, contrast-checked colours, line patterns and direction arrows. Shared sections display every permitted profile; clean/dirty/shared remains defined by route profiles. The searchable table projects explicit and automatic same-floor graph access, combining node and directed-edge allowances with physical directions. Empty lists are unrestricted. Automatic reverse connections retain direction provenance. Lift allowances are listed separately and do not block same-floor transit at lift nodes. Malformed input disables the preview visibly; removed selections switch off. Styles persist per user by profile name without changing project/check/revision/run inputs. Playback uses frozen profile data. Independent directed reference cases, simulator agreement, styling/persistence, map interaction and large-text controls pass.
limitations: This is a permission projection, not a trajectory or feasibility assessment. Direct-travel fallback, task-local additions, combined loads, clearance, outages and timing are not displayed. Lift journeys are not same-floor corridors. Dense labels need zoom/filtering; automatic collision avoidance and standalone legacy viewer controls remain open. Schematic parallel strokes are not verified lanes or swept geometry.

title: Per-user accessible display preferences
contract: Project Appearance provides Light, Dark and High contrast presets, 8-24 pt interface text, 10-28 px layout text, custom text/accent/map colours and a visible or hidden map legend. Preferences persist separately from project/revision/run inputs. Existing standard controls are repolished and new controls inherit the palette/font. Active text is checked at 4.5:1 against preset backgrounds, accent at 3:1; selected text uses whichever of black/white has greater contrast. Invalid drafts do not apply, corrupt settings fall back visibly without overwriting, and failed saves retain active preferences. Apply does not alter project data, history or check currency. Pending property drafts survive. Reference contrast, persistence, live controls, keyboard actions and 1280x800 large-text behaviour are tested.
limitations: Playback map labels, timelines, drawings and some legacy custom controls retain existing rendering. Arbitrary underlays are outside contrast checks. Complete keyboard/screen-reader and dialog coverage, route-profile labels/patterns/colour preferences and accessibility compliance are not established.

title: Explicit recovery of staged containers
contract: A direct recovery task names an exact issued container staged at its pickup and marked as requiring recovery. It claims the container exclusively, applies ordinary robot, route-profile and destination-capacity checks, and moves it at scheduled pickup/dropoff. Rejection restores claims; failed recovery before pickup leaves staging intact, while failure after pickup records unconfirmed arrival. Confirmed arrival preserves physical identity/state and closes the outstanding recovery finding. Tasks UI exposes identity and recovery and preserves unrelated options.
limitations: Recovery is configured for a new run; it does not mutate frozen logs or resume a completed run. No unidentified or unconfirmed object is recovered. Staging geometry/capacity and direct recovery combined with staff handoffs or further automatic returns are unsupported. Existing manual-task robot compatibility rules apply.

title: Same-floor graph routing
contract: Euclidean edge lengths unless distance_m is supplied; directed edges remain directed; distance divided by constant speed gives travel time.
limitations: Reference cases do not prove all graph shapes or validate surveyed distances.

title: Door and corridor straight-passage width
contract: Passage requires max(robot width, oriented payload width) <= effective edge width, with 1e-9 m numerical tolerance. Effective width is the minimum of the corridor and its endpoint door openings. Select the shortest passable route.
limitations: No safety clearance, door height, opening time, door leaf swing or swept turning footprint is modelled. A door restricts both full incident edges.

title: Route profiles and task restrictions
contract: Route profiles define clean, dirty and shared access: shared sections belong to each applicable profile. Profile and task allow-lists are unioned; empty lists mean unrestricted; edge pairs are directed. The dirty task label selects the dirty profile only when no explicit profile is supplied. Unknown effective profiles reject scheduling instead of becoming unrestricted. Empty approach, charging and idle-return travel remain unrestricted by profiles. Returns use return_route_profile or their label fallback; seeded waste returns may inherit the outbound profile. Generating profile edges from selected nodes includes both directions of two-way corridors. Each multi-stop leg intersects the effective permissions of payloads currently onboard; empty intersections remain forbidden. Clearance uses only the oriented payloads currently carried. Profile/task unions remain per-task; batch groups retain profile and dirty-label compatibility.
limitations: No physical contamination-state model or empty-journey profile selector. Task allowances can widen a profile intentionally. Reference node, edge and lift intersections are verified; seeded-return and wider profile interactions remain incomplete. Static checks do not resolve every effective generation or runtime-return profile; the engine checks effective tasks before scheduling. Existing saved edge lists are not automatically changed; regenerate deliberately if reverse directions were omitted.

title: Corridor lane capacity
contract: Current two-way capacity approximation uses half corridor width and both loaded length and width to choose one or two concurrent lanes.
limitations: Not a directional keep-right lane model; no geometric junction conflict or overtaking verification. Length-based lane fitting is conservative.

title: Swept turns and multi-point manoeuvres
contract: Planned shared geometric model with explicit radius, pivot and reversing parameters.
limitations: Existing local manoeuvre drawing uses an approximate radius. Do not treat it as verified full-route swept geometry or steering dynamics.

title: Scheduled generation and override precedence
contract: Global disable wins. Enabled group/department rules can run under disabled category defaults. Group payload overrides category values and suppresses that department's standalone override. Separate groups are separate services. Category-wide zone capacity policy cannot be overridden. Category-only generation runs only without groups or department overrides. Polling includes the final partial interval at the inclusive demand horizon; released work can complete afterward. Clock schedules and timeframe slots now use exact calendar events. Effective pre-start releases are excluded; department opening adjustments can retain an occurrence across midnight. Consumption polling cadence is unchanged.
limitations: Exact release does not imply immediate assignment: resource waits, staff handoffs and configured staggering remain. Minute clock parsing is retained; fractional timeframe slots retain calculated precision. The wider generation-mode and calendar interaction matrix is still incomplete.

title: Consumption, threshold, waste and timeframe generation
contract: Generation derives demand from schedules, configured consumption and department assignments; tracked containers have separate balances.
limitations: Independent boundary cases remain for every mode, recurrence, waste volume, partial-day and timeframe allocation. Preview must distinguish runtime-dependent demand from fixed schedules.

title: Task assignment, priorities and deferral
contract: Deferral deadline starts at the original release and applies until assignment; zero means unlimited. Idle parking is excluded. One reference delivery takes 2 + 10/2 + 2 = 9 seconds.
limitations: Priority fairness, all candidate-limit interactions and end-of-run incomplete-task reconciliation need further reference cases.

title: Returns, staff handoffs and exchanges
contract: Returns and staff transfers retain physical payload identities. Same-container servicing records an arrival outside storage and returns the original bin; finite exchange stock is unaffected. Destination dwell and walking contribute separately to availability.
limitations: Existing regression coverage is broad, but a complete independent return/profile/staff-shift matrix is outstanding.

title: Location reservation capacity
contract: Reservations occupy half-open intervals. A request starts at the earliest time that existing simultaneous occupancy stays below capacity throughout its duration.
limitations: These tests cover location reservations, not all lift, edge, staff or junction contention.

title: Inventory bays and payload instances
contract: Flexible bays accept matching dimensions with permitted plan rotation. Exchange deliveries and returns can represent different physical instances. Same-bin service arrivals do not create stored stock or consume a finite bay. Strict multi-stop deliveries require distinct compatible bays. Existing active claims cannot be overwritten. Temporarily full compatible bays wait until capacity is released or the original deferral deadline expires; without a deadline they can remain pending. Finite full-bin exchange plans claim distinct existing empty instances at commit, retain them in storage until outbound arrival, consume only their owned claim, and release unconsumed claims on rejection or task failure. Physical pickup/dropoff are scheduled independently of journey completion, including batch legs and post-delivery washing; completion fallbacks are idempotent. Equivalent-bin exchange requires an enabled return. Without it, deliveries need ordinary free storage and cannot consume empty stock. Tasks requiring existing source stock claim distinct physical instances at serial route commitment; estimates remain non-binding, rejected commits restore claims and task bindings, and pickup/failure releases owned claims. Exact and empty-only pickups take precedence over flexible selection; source pickups and empty exchanges cannot share an instance. Delivered stock can be collected again. An explicit ID on an ordinary outbound task creates at most one physical object: committed creation is exclusive, issued IDs require existing stock at the requested source, and in-transit or removed objects cannot be recreated. Creation claims roll back or release on failure before pickup. Generated IDs skip registered explicit IDs. Conflicting task payload types for one ID are preflight errors.
limitations: Reference cycles verify instance conservation and storage counts; system-wide conservation over long mixed workflows still needs independent evidence. Explicit staging geometry/capacity remains open. Direct staged recovery is verified in PAYLOAD-RECOVERY-01; unconfirmed locations cannot be recovered. Internal same-bin and staged-equivalent returns retain their existing continuation policies. Lifecycle counts distinguish planned, stored, in-transit, staged, unconfirmed and removed IDs. Physical population peaks include active issued objects; final identity records support state totals. Failed returns preserve staged identities and flag recovery needs. Staff-action timing and full mixed-workflow lifecycle coverage remain incomplete.

title: AMR types, slots and multi-stop routing
contract: Robot and slot dimensions constrain payload compatibility; multi-stop tasks share movements. Each multi-stop leg intersects the effective permissions of payloads currently onboard; empty intersections remain forbidden. Clearance uses only the oriented payloads currently carried. Profile/task unions remain per-task; batch groups retain profile and dirty-label compatibility. Rejected serial multi-stop commits restore touched reservations, inventory claims, lift operational state, battery/energy and impact counters. Rejected individual and idle-return commits also restore task destinations, robot state and appended charging records.
limitations: Slot combinations, fleet contention, routing optimality and all orientation combinations need further cases. Greedy pickup-first stop ordering is not a complete tour search. Swept slot geometry is not verified. Distinct empty-bin claims are verified; atomicity beyond route planning remains a separate audit.

title: Battery, charging and idle returns
contract: Opportunity charging is optional and admits idle robots progressively. Rejected charging-route plans retain departure occupancy and restore charger claims, lift operational state and robot targets. Estimates do not assign a target charger. One in-place charge reference verifies 10 kWh / 2 kW = 18000 seconds. Charger travel reserves corridor capacity, spends 75% of rated motor power over corridor movement, and recharges from arrival energy. Explicit waits consume no traction energy; lift energy is recorded separately and not deducted from the AMR battery on charger trips. Available battery may cross the reserve threshold but cannot be exceeded. The legacy recharge entry point uses charge-cycle events. Delivery and batch traction now uses corridor/local-manoeuvre durations and actual onboard load; explicit waits and lift travel consume no AMR traction. Lift supply includes boarding standby and is recorded once per journey. Exact committed traction must leave the battery reserve intact; estimates do not spend battery. At an operational charger, an individual delivery whose constructed route exceeds current battery but fits a full battery is retried after charging. The abandoned commit is rolled back, then routing and reservations are recomputed at the later time. Charging, pickup/dropoff and completion share one timeline. When no delivery is assignable, an eligible idle robot can request charging for route energy even above reserve. Each available compatible charger is checked for reachable arrival and a feasible full-battery onward task; commitment rechecks the selected destination. The original task stays pending and records route_charge_required evidence. Charger availability inspection is read-only; stale markers are cleaned only during serial claims. Investigation and report analysis share a source-attributed movement ledger: native event IDs count once, and complete bound logs with the energy capability distinguish known zero from missing evidence. Multi-stop task energy is unallocated; shared journey totals remain explicitly labelled. Transport groups containing shared journeys leave task energy blank. PDF lift totals use the same evidence and preserve unknowns. Planned recharge segments record input separately from applied battery credits. Complete bound logs reconcile each expected robot: initial plus applied charge minus traction equals final model energy, with separate counter checks. In-place charge credits occur at route commitment; separate cycles credit on completion. Missing or cancelled evidence remains unknown. Duplicate event IDs count once; conflicting duplicates are rejected. Explicit charger bays are reserved before travel and occupied at arrival. Separate charge-cycle IDs reject stale or duplicate events. Arrival and completion recheck charger validity and ownership; rejected cycles credit no energy. Busy chargers and failed charging attempts are operational events, not delivery task failures. Earlier delivery completions cannot clear a newer charging reservation. Identical local position and heading require zero movement.
limitations: Energy remains approximate: no stationary AMR auxiliary draw or robot own mass in the lift equation; rated-power/load formula is not a measured vehicle model. Fast assignment and pre-charge estimates omit some traffic and local-bay effects; exact individual-route shortfalls now replan in-place charging, and dispatch from non-chargers is covered by bounded references. Direct batch charging now replans the whole tour at the later departure, rolling back the original attempt. Charger detours check the entire onward batch and serial availability. Feasible deliveries precede detours; charged batches retain multi-stop preference among detours. Whole-fleet optimisation remains outstanding. Full-battery infeasibility is a route-attempt finding, not proof that every future route is impossible. One-bay/two-robot contention and fault-injected bay losses are verified. FIFO queues, idle-full-robot relocation, continuously monitored charger faults, partial charge after interruption, efficiency and wider threshold boundaries remain open. Locations without explicit bays retain legacy unbounded charging. Per-task batch energy allocation is deliberately unspecified; use movement events once for journey totals. Energy is route-plan consumption, not independently measured execution, and charging input is excluded from this movement ledger. Legacy logs lack corrected segment attribution. Atomicity after route planning and full report reconciliation remain separate audits.

title: Lift simulation and movement exports
contract: Lift transfers and empty repositioning are distinct movements; multiple tasks on one movement do not multiply its count. Reposition and loaded speeds are sampled at their planned start times. Committed routes remain fixed. Wear/failure-enabled lifts book in chronological commitment order; with both disabled, gaps are allowed only when the new recorded journey restores the next booking's original starting floor. No unrecorded reset movement is assumed. Committed journeys apply wear once; estimates do not. Rejected commits restore wear, repair and reservations. Deterministic failures use accumulated vertical operating time and a post-wear health-scaled threshold; boarding, doors and waits are excluded. Zero threshold disables failures; zero repair time still records a failure. Repair does not restore health; the minimum operating-health boundary is inclusive. Results Investigation checks per-lift recorded floor continuity and exclusive movement intervals, with a 2 ms rounding tolerance, against frozen initial floors and booking-derived transfer/reposition counts. Conflicts link to native events; full known-zero coverage requires the new count capability and valid complete evidence. Legacy or filtered observations remain explicitly incomplete.
limitations: Commitment-order scheduling can leave gaps unused and can delay a robot behind an already booked later arrival. Dynamic replanning of committed journeys is not implemented. Mid-phase outage/speed integration, multiple-lift interactions, stochastic failures and complete report reconciliation remain unverified or unsupported. Health and repair state represent committed work rather than elapsed-time sensor state. Project Checks exposes these scheduling and reliability assumptions.

title: People movement and congestion
contract: Configured people occupancy applies speed factors to corridor travel.
limitations: No dedicated independent reference suite for overlapping profiles, ramp shapes or time windows yet.

title: Scenarios and resource availability
contract: Scenario events modify selected resource availability and speed over configured periods. Scheduled boundaries wake pending work and invalidate estimates. Individual, batch and separate charging admission respect robot outages. Structural lift feasibility is independent of temporary availability. Windows are half-open and overnight weekdays belong to the start day; equal clocks mean all day. Original task deferral deadlines remain in force.
limitations: Already committed work is not interrupted. Mid-journey outages, chained corridor closures, lift repair/wear, speed-only interactions, DST and full malformed-input validation remain outstanding. Partial availability retains a speed-factor approximation, not stochastic uptime. Recovery boundaries are limited to the configured demand horizon.

title: Run period and simulation time
contract: Simulation times are elapsed seconds relative to the configured start datetime. Individual exports may round times.
limitations: Timezone/DST, all midnight boundaries and all end-of-run semantics need explicit policy and reference cases. tick_rate is not a physical accuracy setting.

title: Reports and metric reconciliation
contract: Tasks, AMR journeys, payload movements and lift trips are separate measures. Missing metadata must not be fabricated.
limitations: Complete metric-to-event traceability and reconciliation for every report measure remain outstanding.

title: PDF/DXF drawing import and export
contract: Drawings provide floor-scaled underlays; topology uses explicit world coordinates.
limitations: No automatic verified obstacle extraction from drawings. Broader import failure/scale coverage remains.

title: Editor validation and dialog behaviour
contract: Structured preflight reports severity, object, consequences and navigation; edits invalidate reports and acknowledgements. Launcher snapshots checked inputs and warnings per run. Existing dialogs remain available. Shared compressed edit history supports undo/redo of completed configuration and canvas edits.
limitations: Incremental checks, not a complete schema. Generation rule references need effective precedence resolution; legacy findings may lack exact navigation. Undo groups existing dialogs and callbacks; individual command migration and systematic accessibility coverage remain outstanding.

title: Visualiser and task investigation
contract: Playback uses event records; failure navigation locates the affected destination.
limitations: Legacy playback remains supported. Results investigation adds evidence IDs and task timelines; shared swept trajectories and full report reconciliation remain outstanding.

title: Portable project, history and integrated application
contract: Compressed .amrproj stores deduplicated drawings and revisions with atomic saves and restore. Separate 30-second recovery copies preserve unsaved configurations and available drawings; Save/Discard/Cancel protects open/close. JSON export serves existing tools; results remain external. Project runs saves, checks and simulates a frozen saved revision in a separate process, with external results bound to project, revision and software identities. Optional versioned archive metadata persists external results roots and run references without embedding outputs or creating configuration revisions. Accepted new runs and relinks save atomically. Relative paths support moving a project/results bundle; Save As rebases links to existing folders. Missing references remain visible; relinking validates the selected run, revision/configuration and software identities. Metadata saves preserve unsaved configuration edits. Older archives without links open unchanged. A persistent workflow tree hosts Project, Layout, Configuration, Check, Simulate, Review and Report in one central workspace. Existing checks, demand, history, run and investigation panels are reused against shared state. Selected runs flow into investigation and reporting. Reports verify full bound logs and frozen inputs, run in a separate process, retain source/report software checksums, and remain external. Cancelled or failed reports cannot be opened as completed outputs. Review embeds revision-bound playback with a local timeline and monitors, read-only background loading, native event identities, independent reference positions, and stale-selection/project-switch guards. Playback pauses on leaving the workspace. Current edits cannot change frozen run inputs. Layout has a searchable object tree and contextual position, door, corridor and location-wash properties. Changed fields apply atomically with bulk previews and one-step undo; valid drafts are included in recovery. Stale drafts cannot overwrite newer edits. Robots, payloads, lifts, static tasks and route profiles have tree entries and common contextual fields. Route permissions use searchable node, directed-edge and lift selections, with explicit unrestricted-empty semantics. Untouched nested settings and identities are preserved. Lift speed edits synchronize floors/s with the legacy m/s representation.
limitations: Playback drawing underlays, interruptible/paged large-log loading, nested configuration editing and object creation/deletion/renaming, broader identity/floor editing, removal/retention controls and large-project responsiveness remain outstanding. Configuration tools still use existing dialogs. Report generation is integrated, but PDF viewing uses the system viewer and complete metric reconciliation remains open. Storage/discovery operations are synchronous. Older builds may discard optional metadata; complete migration coverage remains open. The legacy launcher retains its machine-specific workspace path.

title: Demand preview and rule provenance
contract: Frozen planned-task preview with filters, timetable, effective rule settings, no-work explanations and simple independent schedule reconciliation. Runtime-dependent totals remain unknown.
limitations: Complex calendars, runtime inventory/returns and full waste field-source attribution are not independently verified. Preview IDs are not simulation event IDs.

title: Results timelines and run evidence
contract: Recorded task outcomes and metric definitions link to contributing events. New logs retain stable event/journey identities, frozen inputs and source fingerprints; old logs expose missing evidence. Completed and failed task sets reconcile with bound run summaries. Payload service arrivals close transfers without adding inventory; logs declare this capability so older logs do not claim zero service activity. Failures after pickup and before dropoff record an unconfirmed physical arrival; no source stock or destination arrival is fabricated. Failed batch members cannot later complete. New full logs publish final lifecycle identities; investigation metrics link state and issued totals to those records. Missing lifecycle evidence remains unknown. Report task counts are independent of physical IDs; missing ID or physical-population evidence is not substituted with task or stored counts. Results Investigation checks per-lift recorded floor continuity and exclusive movement intervals, with a 2 ms rounding tolerance, against frozen initial floors and booking-derived transfer/reposition counts. Conflicts link to native events; full known-zero coverage requires the new count capability and valid complete evidence. Legacy or filtered observations remain explicitly incomplete.
limitations: Planned segments do not prove execution. Payload pairing can be incomplete; wait causes are not additive; full PDF metric reconciliation and large-log pagination remain open.

title: Corridor drawing, splitting and subdivision
contract: Selected explicit same-floor corridors can be divided into 2–100 sections, or split at a projected click. Directed edges share inserted nodes and retain attributes. Configured distance is divided proportionally; geometric paths stay on the original line. Route-profile and task allowances, people corridor references and scenario corridor resources are updated atomically. Original doors stay at their endpoints. One undo restores the complete configuration. Clean/dirty/shared access remains defined by route profiles. Continuous drawing previews and atomically places, reuses or joins points, automatically linking each click with per-step undo. Point/edge snapping precedes grid rounding. Finishing or changing floor/mode/history clears the active chain. New links honor the bidirectional choice; existing links retain their permissions. New branches are not implicitly granted restricted profile access.
limitations: Added graph sections can change reservation and people-occupancy timing; identical congested outcomes are not promised. Auto-generated links must first be explicit. Crossing lines do not implicitly join; an overlapping target selects one corridor, not all crossings. Configurable snap tolerances, dedicated crossing operations, geometric traffic and all effective generated-rule interactions remain open. Historical links are not migrated for the former direction-checkbox defect.
